title: Connected exposition, praise and figurative language
prior_teaching_boundary: Only the sixteen active contracts and actual registers at defa800 establish teaching. Recognition and supplied exposure remain distinct from production; no archived milestones are inherited.
productive_outcomes: Produce every assigned productive cell of the selected complete nominal, adjectival and verbal systems, applying the evidenced stem changes, endings, exceptions and bounded senses together.
Keep each complete clause's subject, object, recipient and internal relative role distinct across comparison, report, condition, coordination and participial expansion.
Distinguish second-person commands, third-person wishes and statements in praise, blessing and petition; retain each original Cook omission, lexical and word-order control.

Use the specifically assigned nominalized adjective and participial frames with their own case roles and governed dependents; do not derive unrestricted substantival syntax merely from prior adjectival morphology.
Interpret equality, greater degree, comparison of actions, metaphor and simile without replacing the literal structure by an unsupported paraphrase.

Use each explicitly taught new lexical sense and government, including familiar-headword meanings that the actual prior register does not establish; use printed local help for deliberately supplied expressions.

Translate all 82 unchanged Cook joint XII, XIII.37–43 prompts, retaining every clause, enumerated member, participant and stated control; distinguish valid Old English from compliance with a narrower exercise target.
recognition_outcomes: Translate the complete252word music-performance episode with its local help, from the daughter's performance through the criticism, demonstration and audience response.
Trace the speaker, addressee, antecedents and grammatical roles through the nested reports and compare a reported belief with a narrator's assertion.
Explain the source's bounded figurative and performance meanings from the actual Old English and supplied notes; preserve its printed variants and number choices.
Distinguish a source quotation, an exact English prompt, a documented normalization, supplied reading help and new teaching material.
Recognize that an exact dictionary hint or displayed frame is an input/reference position; using it correctly does not certify its independent recall.

explicit_limits: Only the actual sixteen active coverage contracts and actual registers at the coordinator's defa800 baseline establish prior teaching. No archived-course milestone is imported.

The baseline has 1,067 lemmas, 11,188 forms, 1,376 senses, and 1,080 features. Form, sense and construction knowledge are independent records; a matching string or familiar lemma does not close all three dependencies.

All 82 numbered prompts remain under the joint XII, XIII heading, with original IDs and English prompts unchanged except the source audit's declared typography normalization. No item-level redistribution is currently proposed.

Exercise 37's global omission of the article and second-person pronoun applies to its complete set; it does not prohibit third-person subjects in wishes or create a universal Old English article rule.

Complete tables display all literal assigned cells with productive/reference/supplied status. Complete noun classes include both singular and plural; a proper name, plural ethnonym or genuinely bounded system has its evidence-supported shape, without fabricated cells.
An abstract/mass sense's reference plural does not grant a new count meaning. A full verbal system grants only the expressly stated moods, tense series, nonfinite forms and lexical frames.

The high quantities in 39.2 and 42.2 require complete visible phrase help unless the reconciled contract deliberately teaches a full bounded numeral system. They cannot become independent recall tests from bare English prompts.

Negative knowing in 43.8 can use verified ne plus positive witan; no nytan paradigm is introduced merely because the English proposition is negative. The source's exact nāst in 174.18 remains separately classified.
Literal wǣre in 38.9 is a visible original hint. Its contextual comparative use needs explanation but does not by itself establish a universal comparative-subjunctive rule.

The checked reading is 174.7–175.17, a coherent episode within A Lesson in Music. Individual lines are editorial counts anchored by printed marginal numbers. The intervening earlier feast and later love/gifts paragraph are not newly assigned.

All 19 original notes and 20 anchors remain separate from modern help. A note's Latin corroboration supports interpretation but does not replace the actual Old English text or create an extra Latin translation task.

Source-specific expressions, proper-name spellings and deliberately supplied Cook frames remain visible during assessment. Supply their actual forms, local sense and argument structure together; never test unsupported independent recollection.

Four short new translated examples have exact prior form/sense/feature bindings. No additional connected invented narrative is proposed. Five original morphology groups contain 21 explicit outputs with exact system and dependency bindings.
Current proposals and all author-only models are excluded from the fresh blind learner solver until every actual requested output is attempted and frozen.
bounded_scope.assessment_boundary: Visible Cook hints and all supplied whole frames, local forms and contextual senses remain visible during their tasks. Their component recall is never independently assessed.
bounded_scope.source_reading: One complete 252-word performance episode at 174.7–175.17; all 19 original notes and 20 anchors retained. The following love and gifts are not assigned.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Masculine consonant stems43: singular zero/es/e/zero; plural as/a/um/as. Do not infer gender or class merely from an English translation.

Syncope43.4 requires a heavy initial and light second syllable in the stated model; compare ēðel→ēðles with hęngest retaining e. Noun classes and explicitly listed exceptions outrank a mechanical spelling rule.

Neuter47 nominative/accusative plural takes u for the stated short monosyllabic model, zero for the heavy model. Disyllables and compounds need their own diagnostic statement rather than automatic assignment from a final spelling. Cook47.1 explicitly lists mægnu in nominative/accusative plural; the selected table retains mægen- in all oblique forms. Final long vowels/diphthongs and consonant clusters matter, including palmtwīg and nest.
Feminine51.5 -nes/-en/-el/-et doubles the final consonant in oblique forms and retains e. Explicit examples and glossary assignments govern cnēoris and ðīnen.
Weak53 m-a/f-e: oblique singular an, plural an/ena/um/an. Weak neuter ēare keeps e in nominative/accusative singular and has genitive plural ēarna.
Strong/weak adjective choice is a syntactic choice. Substantival use is separately identified; familiar adjective forms do not automatically teach a new lexical meaning or new participial government.

Tables are complete only within their named number/sense and case scope. Singular-only teaching is an assignment boundary, never an assertion that the word is defective. Supplied source forms must be visible at the task and cannot be independent-recall targets.

Direct-address adjectives take weak forms under Cook55 and prior u09-vocative-weak-adjective. Thus the selected address forms are wæstmbǣran, gefiðredan, geongan and ealdan. Eall has its separately taught quantifier pattern; its presence does not make every neighboring modifier strong.

audit_recommendation_precedence: This reconciled contract assigns teaching. Audit proposals supply evidence; complete morphology does not establish every sense or construction.

source_lines.source_with_note_markers: Ðā ēode hēo ūt,[9] and hēt fęccean hiere hearpan. And
sōna swā hēo hearpian ongan, hēo mid wynsumum sange
gemęngde ðǣre hearpan swēg. Ðā ongunnon ealle ðā
męnn hīe hęrian on hiere swēgcræfte; and Apollonius
āna[10] swīgode. Ðā cwæð se cyning: “Apolloni, nū ðū
dēst[11] yfele, for-ðǣm-ðe ealle męnn hęriað mīne dohtor
on hiere swēgcræfte,[12] and ðū āna hīe, swīgende,[12a] tǣlst.[13]”
Apollonius cwæð: “Ēalā, ðū gōda cyning, gif ðū mē
gelīefst,[14] ic sęcge ðæt ic ongiete ðæt sōðlice ðīn dohtor
gefēoll[15] on swēgcræft, ac hēo næfð hine nā wel geleornod;
ac hāt mē[16] nū sęllan ðā hearpan, ðonne wāst[17] ðū nū ðæt
ðū gīet nāst.[17]” Arcestrates se cyning cwæð: “Apolloni,
ic oncnāwe sōðlice ðæt ðū eart[1] on eallum ðingum wel
gelǣred.”
Ðā hēt se cyning sęllan Apollonie ðā hearpan. Apol-
lonius ðā ūtēode, and hine scrȳdde, and sętte ænne
cynehelm upon his hēafod, and nōm ðā hearpan on his
hand, and inēode, and swā stōd ðæt se cyning and ealle
ðā ymbsittendan wēndon ðæt hē nǣre Apollonius, ac ðæt
hē wǣre Apollines,[2] ðāra hǣðenra god. Ðā wearð stilnes
and swīge[3] geworden innan ðǣre healle. And Apollonius
his hearpenægl genōm, and hē ðā hearpestręngas mid
cræfte āstyrian ongan, and ðǣre hearpan swēg mid wyn-
sumum sange gemęngde.[4] And se cyning self, and ealle
ðe ðǣr andwearde wǣron, micelre stefne cleopedon and
hine hęredon. Æfter ðisum forlēt[5] Apollonius ðā hearpan,
and[6] plegode, and fela fægerra ðinga[7] ðǣr forðtēah,[8] ðe
ðǣm folce ungecnāwen wæs and ungewunelic. And him[9]
eallum ðearle līcode ǣlc ðāra ðinga ðe hē forðtēah.

Ðā ongunnon ealle ðā męnn hīe hęrian on hiere swēgcræfte; and Apollonius āna swīgode. Ðā cwæð se cyning: “Apolloni, nū ðū dēst yfele, for-ðǣm-ðe ealle męnn hęriað mīne dohtor on hiere swēgcræfte, and ðū āna hīe, swīgende, tǣlst.” Apollonius cwæð: “Ēalā, ðū gōda cyning, gif ðū mē gelīefst, ic sęcge ðæt ic ongiete ðæt sōðlice ðīn dohtor gefēoll on swēgcræft, ac hēo næfð hine nā wel geleornod; ac hāt mē nū sęllan ðā hearpan, ðonne wāst ðū nū ðæt ðū gīet nāst.” Arcestrates se cyning cwæð: “Apolloni, ic oncnāwe sōðlice ðæt ðū eart on eallum ðingum wel gelǣred.” Ðā hēt se cyning sęllan Apollonie ðā hearpan. Apollonius ðā ūtēode, and hine scrȳdde, and sętte ænne cynehelm upon his hēafod, and nōm ðā hearpan on his hand, and inēode, and swā stōd ðæt se cyning and ealle ðā ymbsittendan wēndon ðæt hē nǣre Apollonius, ac ðæt hē wǣre Apollines, ðāra hǣðenra god. Ðā wearð stilnes and swīge geworden innan ðǣre healle. And Apollonius his hearpenægl genōm, and hē ðā hearpestręngas mid cræfte āstyrian ongan, and ðǣre hearpan swēg mid wynsumum sange gemęngde. And se cyning self, and ealle ðe ðǣr andwearde wǣron, micelre stefne cleopedon and hine hęredon. Æfter ðisum forlēt Apollonius ðā hearpan, and plegode, and fela fægerra ðinga ðǣr forðtēah, ðe ðǣm folce ungecnāwen wæs and ungewunelic. And him eallum ðearle līcode ǣlc ðāra ðinga ðe hē forðtēah.

teaching_records.description: The selected geong, eald, mihtig, ēaðmōd and rīce adjectives can name groups of people. U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.

U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.locator_convention: Original separately served facsimiles; a/b denote left/right printed columns. No local PDF pagination.
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.verification: Both original pages directly viewed; online entry used as a finding aid. Quantities/spelling in examples are BT’s own and are not silently converted to Cook.
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.claim: The entry distinguishes uninflected participles from inflected and mixed usage with habban. The object may be described by an accusative participle; the finite auxiliary still agrees with its subject. Bare and agreeing realizations are evidenced alternatives, not an exceptionless mapping from English perfect grammar.

exact_examples.analysis: Plural finite subject Hie contrasts with singular accusative hine/ofslægenne. This is evidence for object-linked participial inflection, not participle agreement with the finite subject.

exact_examples.text: Ðú hafast helle bereáfod and ðæs deáþes aldor gebundenne
exact_examples.analysis: The coordinated example combines a bare participle with an inflected accusative-masculine participle referring to the object aldor.

U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.evidence_limits: Use the selected bare bases for Unit12 production. U16-MT-P114.inspection_scope: Firstcolumn14.8: Iohannes heafod þæs fulluhteres. Firstcolumn14.10: beheafdode Iohannem on þam cwerterne. The genitive Iohannes and accusative Iohannem are directly attested; the rightcolumn variant Iohanne is not silently substituted.
U16-MT-P114.declared_normalization: Retain the attested endings, writing initial J in Johannes/Johannem solely to follow Cook’s printed Johannes hint. No vowel quantity is inferred and no complete Latin proper-name system is assigned.
U16-MT-P114.teaching_scope: Supply Johannes as the genitive in36.9 and Johannem as the accusative in36.10; identify both roles explicitly.

U16-C06-REWARD.inspection_scope: The printed weak headword/class belong to a verb meaning sin or fail in duty. Repay/reward requires the distinct strong gyldan verb. The source English, original hint and original image are all retained; only modern guidance is corrected.

supporting_primary_evidence.observation: Strong a-gildan/-geldan/-gieldan/-gyldan has geald/guldon/golden and includes reward, repay, requite. Separate weak a-giltan has gilte/gilt and means sin, fail, do wrong.
a-gyldan expressly gives thu gyltst/he gylt and geald/guldon/golden. Dative recipients occur in repayment examples. Separate a-gyltan/-giltan has gylte/gilte and gylt/gilt, fail in duty or sin.
Reward is the noun med; requite is forgieldan(III.104). The vocabulary supplies no independent support for agyltan as the verb reward.
Strong gieldan/geald/guldon/golden is explicitly tabulated under104. Prefixing does not turn this into weak class113.
Section113 describes weak de/te preterits retaining the stem vowel, with hieran, fyllan, cyssan, settan and sendan among its examples. It cannot describe strong gyldan/geald/guldon/golden.

Print every introduced complete system with governing endings, stems, alternations, exceptions and sense/number limits. Any prior complete model must have an exact visible teaching and derivation route.
Teach every independently required form, sense and construction before first use; keep supplied support visible at the task. Prior exposure alone does not establish production.

Retain the exact 252-word reading, 19 original notes and 20 anchors. Preserve uncertainty, negation, source-specific constructions and quotation punctuation; explain them without silent normalization.
Four translated examples and the contracted original tasks are new teaching material; no additional narrative is composed. Source questions become tasks only when explicitly assigned.
Provide a separate key for every requested output with model, target, essential meaning, explanation, defensible alternatives and useful diagnosis. Distinguish valid language from a stated target.
A fresh non-author freezes every actual solution in Git before explicit key/current-contract/audit/model access. A separate fresh reviewer checks complete paradigms against primary evidence.

Resolve material findings, export complete learner/key PDFs, check full content parity and obtain non-author inspection of every final page. Preserve prior artifacts and records, update indexes, export Beads and commit locally. Do not draft Unit 18.

methods: Actual sixteen-unit registers and coverage contracts read before proposals; historical archive grants no teaching credit.

review_independence_protocol.main_reviewer: Fresh non-author to be assigned after complete drafts
review_independence_protocol.blind_phase: Solve every actual learner task from student.md and its visible teaching and support. Read the sixteen earlier active coverage contracts and actual cumulative registers as required by AGENTS.md; earlier accepted learner chapters may also be consulted. Initial allowlist: the current learner master, earlier active coverage contracts, accepted earlier learner materials and actual registers, original primary images or scans without current editorial annotation, AGENTS.md, EDITORIAL_POLICY.md and this neutral protocol. Do not open the current coverage contract, brief, audits, proposals, source token maps, key, ordered models, complete translation witnesses or helpers exposing them. An audit filename need not say private to contain answers.
review_independence_protocol.freeze_gate: Coordinator verifies every actual requested output is attempted, records learner identity, exports Beads and commits the unchanged witness locally. Only the coordinator's subsequent explicit message unlocks comparison. Elapsed time or files appearing do not unlock it.
review_independence_protocol.comparison_phase: Compare every frozen solution with the separate key, actual requested output positions, target versus validity distinctions, evidence and exact assigned dependencies. Keep the initial witness immutable; record corrections and disagreements separately. Resolve all material findings and bind acceptance to final actual masters and substantive contract identity.
review_independence_protocol.paradigm_reviewer: Separate fresh non-author agent: inspect every actual complete display, diagnostics and derivations against primary evidence; check the exact forms, senses, frames and scope. Structural equality alone is not linguistic proof.
review_independence_protocol.exclusive_files: Reviewers edit only their allocated review files; the coordinator owns contract and integration, and authors own lesson/key repairs.
review_independence_protocol.known_exposure: Root, unit17_source, unit17_grammar and unit17_design have current audit or design roles and are ineligible to claim a fresh blind solve of this unit.
review_independence_protocol.page_review: Every final learner/key page requires non-author visual inspection bound to final PDF and rendered-image identities. Byte-identical reuse must identify the actual earlier inspected image; hashing alone is not inspection.
review_independence_protocol.external_help_boundary: If a task needs external lookup because the actual learner teaching/help omits a dependency, record a dependency gap even if a primary source enables a correct answer. Primary access does not silently cure missing learner support.
